hypothesis: Weights in an S3 Express One Zone directory bucket in the function's AZ have a lower time to first byte and higher throughput than an S3 general-purpose bucket, so the weight-download phase of a cold start (and of each SnapStart snapshot init) is shorter, while deserialize, model init and inference are unchanged.

changed_variable.name: weights bucket type
changed_variable.baseline: S3 general-purpose bucket, S3 Standard (arm gp; also gpv in the VPC)
changed_variable.experiment: S3 Express One Zone directory bucket in use2-az1 (arm xz; also xzv in a use2-az1 VPC subnet)

deployment.az: directory bucket in use2-az1. Arms gp and xz are not VPC-attached, so Lambda picks each execution environment's AZ (unobservable); arms gpv and xzv run in one private use2-az1 subnet, so xzv is guaranteed same-AZ

model.transform: LoRA merged fp32 (weights/merge_export.py), H512 Hadamard fold (weights/fold_hadamard.py --block 512)

conditions.weight_fetch: HEAD + parallel 64 MiB ranged GETs (32 threads) into a memfd (examples/lambda/app/loader.py); llama.cpp mmaps /proc/self/fd/N

classification.method: expected class from the harness (new $LATEST config -> cold; new published version -> restore; reused environment -> warm), checked against REPORT (Init Duration / Restore Duration / neither)

instrumentation_overhead.method: not measured here: every E1 arm is instrumented; P1 measured the overhead (baseline/results/20261020T080835Z)

cost.s3_transfer_note: S3 to Lambda in the same region: no data transfer charge

s3_prices.source: AWS Price List API, AmazonS3, regionCode=us-east-2, 2026-10-20

correctness.method: complete answer object, same request id and same CPU part as the reference

reproduce: git fetch https://github.com/jsamuel1/strands-decider lkai/d654-s3-express && git checkout <commit of this file>
AWS_PROFILE=<profile> SOURCE=s3://<bucket holding P1's weights/ and code/ objects> examples/lambda-kleidiai/e1-s3-express/run_e1.sh <run-id>
conclusion: Small download gain without a VPC; none when the AZ is held fixed; more expensive. Not recommended. Run 20261020T1235Z-e1: 4 arms interleaved over 5 rounds; 2,400 invocations, 0 errors, 0 class mismatches. Correctness: the GGUF sha256 8dbb8872 was read back identical from both buckets, and all 2,400 answers are bit-identical to P1's reference (0 choice flips). No VPC (xz - gp, the headline): cold weight_download p50 24.20 vs 24.95 s (-0.76 s, -3.0%), faster in 5/5 rounds; the control arm's per-round range is 0.18 s. p95 24.31 vs 25.19 s; p99 24.36 vs 28.56 s; 81.9 vs 79.4 MiB/s. Snapshot-init download p50 23.84 vs 24.92 s (n=10 each). Cold first request total -0.72 s (35.17 vs 35.89 s, -2.0%). Same AZ in a use2-az1 VPC subnet (xzv - gpv): weight_download 25.11 vs 25.10 s (+0.07%), 3/5 rounds: no effect. Both VPC arms ran at ~79 MiB/s, so the ~80 MiB/s per-environment ceiling (32 Python threads into a memfd) holds whichever bucket serves the bytes, and Express's lower first-byte latency does not show. The no-VPC gain is therefore not explained by AZ locality. It may come from the zonal endpoint's network path, and it is the only contrast that improved. VPC confound: gpv - gp +0.14 s download and +0.14 s cold first request (Init Duration unchanged); xzv - xz +0.92 s. Compute unchanged: model_load_mmap -0.001 s and first_request_inference +0.000 s (xz - gp). Warm and restore deltas follow the Graviton mix, not the bucket: warm per CPU part is 0.615-0.624 s on 0xd40 for every arm. Restores read no weights. Cost per 1,000 cold starts (Lambda duration + S3): gp $4.96, xz $6.14 (+24%). S3's share is $0.013 vs $1.25 because Express charges $0.0006/GB retrieval on 2.08 GB per download; the 0.76 s saved is worth ~$0.05 of Lambda duration per 1,000. Storage costs $0.23/month for xz vs $0.05 for gp. This run cost $4.91, mostly the SnapStart cache 3-hour minimum. A first attempt (20261020T1130Z-e1) was aborted in round 0: stale pooled HTTPS connections in the benchmark client caused 900 s read timeouts on 10 restore invokes that never reached Lambda. bench_e1.py opens a fresh client per wave. Status 'improved' comes from the pre-registered rule on the headline contrast alone. The same-AZ null result and the cost increase mean it should not be adopted.

e1.status_rule: every round faster; pooled -3.04% beyond noise 0.499 s

arms.gp: general-purpose bucket, no VPC (P1's configuration, E1's own bucket)
arms.xz: S3 Express One Zone directory bucket in the deployment AZ, no VPC (AZ of each execution environment unknown)
arms.gpv: general-purpose bucket, VPC subnet in the deployment AZ, S3 gateway endpoint
arms.xzv: directory bucket, same subnet, S3 Express gateway endpoint (same AZ guaranteed)
